chunks: Concerning a slave who falsely accuses a free person, he said: “He is flogged with the hadd, except for one lash or two lashes.”

So this report may be understood to mean by false accusation something that did not reach the level of qadhf; for that does not make the full hadd obligatory, and ta'zir is required in it. What clarifies what we have mentioned is that Muhammad ibn Muslim has narrated contrary to this, in agreement with the reports we presented earlier.

key_terms.اَلتَّعْزِيرُ: discretionary disciplinary punishment short of the fixed hadd
key_terms.اَلْحَدَّ: the fixed legal punishment prescribed in sacred law
key_terms.اَلْحُرِّ: the free person against whom the false accusation is made
key_terms.اَلْعَبْدِ: the slave; the legally subordinate person discussed in the ruling
key_terms.اَلْقَذْفَ: a specific form of accusatory slander carrying hadd implications
key_terms.يَفْتَرِي: falsely accuses or fabricates a lie against someone
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is flogged; a corporal legal punishment is administered

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith interpret the punishment for a slave who falsely accuses a free person?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling concerning false accusation by a slave against a free person and explores how the report may be interpreted. It explains that the wording may refer to a lesser form of slander short of qadhf, for which ta'zir applies rather than the complete hadd, and notes another narration supporting that understanding.
